description:
About the Position

Griffith University (Australia) is offering a fully funded PhD position for highly motivated students interested in the intersection of conservation genomics, molecular ecology, population genetics, and biodiversity conservation.

The project is led by Dr. Natalie Jones (Ecology) and Dr. Dan Bock (Molecular Ecology) within the School of Environment and Science / Australian Rivers Institute.

Research Focus

Work with cutting-edge technologies including high-quality reference genome assembly, whole-genome resequencing, population genomics, bioinformatics pipelines, and conservation genetic analyses to study the Southern Pink Underwing Moth (Phyllodes imperialis smithersi), one of Australia's most endangered insects, and inform targeted recovery efforts.

The research will generate the first genomics dataset for the Southern Pink Underwing Moth, an endangered insect restricted to fragmented subtropical rainforests in northern NSW and southern Queensland. The work combines genetics, ecology, and molecular ecology to assess genetic diversity, inbreeding, long-term effective population size, and conservation priorities across the species' range.

This PhD is collaborative, involving Bioplatforms Australia, Invertebrates Australia, and the NSW Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW). The project aims to inform habitat protection, rainforest regeneration, and possible genetic rescue or translocation decisions for this priority endangered invertebrate.

Eligible Backgrounds

  • Conservation Genomics
  • Molecular Ecology
  • Population Genetics
  • Bioinformatics
  • Evolutionary Biology
  • Related Fields

Required Skills

  • Strong interest in conservation genomics and biodiversity
  • Background in molecular biology and/or bioinformatics
  • Experience with genomic data analysis (asset)
  • Programming skills in R or Python (asset)
  • Strong analytical and communication skills

Eligibility Highlights

Applicants should have a background in genetics and/or ecology and have achieved a first-class honours degree or a master's degree.

Funding

Full funding including tuition fees and living expenses is available for this position. The scholarship covers all educational costs and provides a monthly stipend.

The successful candidate will need to apply for a Griffith University Postgraduate Research Scholarship to support their stipend for three years of full-time study. The GUPRS provides a living allowance of AUD $35,656 (2026 rate, indexed annually) per annum, paid as a fortnightly stipend.

Application Process

Interested candidates should contact the supervisors for more information:

  • Dan Bock (dan.bock@griffith.edu.au)
  • Natalie Jones (natalie.jones@griffith.edu.au)

Required documents will be specified upon inquiry.

Application dates

  • Contact supervisors directly for application details.
  • Expressions of interest for Griffith University scholarship rounds close in April and September annually.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: 1 September 2026. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
